correctness.rationale: For Y_i=Z_i², decompose first n terms as T W_i with T~chi²_n and W~Dirichlet(1/2,...,1/2) independent. Then S=T² V_n and Δ=(q/m)(T/n−T′/q), with T′ independent chi²_q; conditionally beta_hat-beta=σG/(T sqrt(V_n)). T negative moments are finite iff exponent<n/2, and V_n^-r/2 near the interior barycenter iff r<n−1; this yields slope exponent r<n/2 and the n>=3 sharp tail constant. Conditional unbiasedness holds for n>=3, while T^-1 divergence destroys integrability for n=2 and T^-2 gives variance cutoff n>=5 (V^-1 also finite then). Total variance gives stated formula; independent sympy verifies rational simplification 2(n²+nq+4q)/[n²q(n−2)(n−4)] and corresponding gain threshold. The exact all-integer assertion follows from factorization and polar integrability, not MC checks.
residual_risks: Neither independent exact symbolic algebra nor finite Monte Carlo replaces reasoning at singular T=0 and W barycenter; those are explicitly addressed analytically.

evidence: Rex–Qian optimum multifidelity allocations use stable/population coefficients; Yang–Ding derive asymptotic regression properties, not the finite-pilot negative moments.

originality.rationale: The two-phase regression estimator itself is classical (Yang–Ding eq. 1); the assessed candidate is its exact heavy-tail, moment and MSE law when the same fitted slope is reused with chi-square-one auxiliary response. Earlier nested MFMC papers give optimal population coefficients or warnings about fitted variance but not the inspected exact cutoff n=5 and K_n criterion. Best-of-knowledge with explicit prior regression-literature risk.
residual_risks: Older two-phase sampling literature, including Sitter 1997, may contain an equivalent exact Gaussian-auxiliary specialization not visible from accessible abstract.
The n>=5 cutoff is for shifted Gaussian squares with same-sample unregularized slope, not universal regression or multifidelity estimators.

value.rationale: A precise small-pilot failure mode for a natural noisy quadratic auxiliary variable: exact unbiasedness can coexist with infinite variance, and the exact five-pair cutoff and fit-correction gain criterion are practical finite-sample invariants of a standard two-phase regression construction. The example is motivated by pilot reuse and ill-conditioned slope estimates, not an arbitrary distributional slice.
residual_risks: No general theorem for nonquadratic or non-Gaussian covariates or all pilot-reuse algorithms.
